tldr: Google DeepMind launched Gemini 3.8 Live with an Extended Thinking mode on September 15, adding real-time reasoning to the 3.8 line's voice and video agent capabilities.
whats_new: DeepMind shipped two new Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech models, gemini-3.8-flash-tts and gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts, with a library of over 2,000 voices, and Simon Willison had a playground for trying them live the same day.
why_it_matters: A Flash-tier TTS pair with a low-latency lite variant gives agent builders a cheaper voice layer to pair with 3.8's reasoning modes without leaving the Gemini API.

beats.headline: Gemini 3.8 Live ships with an Extended Thinking mode
Two new Gemini 3.8 TTS models ship with 2,000+ voices
Simon Willison ships a playground for the new TTS voices

open_questions: Do the new TTS models support streaming synthesis for real-time voice agents, or batch-only output?
How does gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts's latency and per-character cost compare to competing low-latency TTS APIs?
take_for_builders: Building a voice agent on Gemini: try gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts on latency-sensitive paths and the full flash-tts for voice variety, and use Willison's playground to audition voices before wiring up the API.
